what_happened: Job 20261107-212343-z26k ("Hold a line after two non-landed attempts instead of retrying it", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 5 of 5 the critic still said the plan needed revising. It confirmed the plan matched the request and reading, that the functions it names exist (with small line drift), and that the demonstrations use real seams. One major finding remained. The plan decides whether the host took a job by checking that a pull-request link exists and a landing record is missing. It ignores the link's own `state` field, which records whether the host merged the job. Landing records come from the local records branch and read as empty when that branch is missing, so jobs that did land could be counted as unlanded. Minor findings: the check at the top of each loop iteration would also refuse the free landing retry of the item's own blocked job, and the dependents list omits the production RealSteps callers in main.rs. One nit on line numbers. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that named seams exist, but does not make the plan trace each classification claim ("the host did not take this job") through the code and records that produce the evidence. Here the existing PR link `state` field and the empty-records-branch behavior would have answered it by reading pr.rs and store.rs. The plan also sets a loop-top check without walking the neighboring existing path, the free landing retry of a blocked job, and misses callers outside the named files. The core flow is the drain, where records, links and gates interact. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step for gaps the code can answer, so one major finding in the last round loses all planning spend. This is the same family as the earlier drain-change cases: the same kind of drain-stop or hold change has now failed planning several times in this way.
prevention: Add a repair step to planning for code-answerable findings. When the last round still has only findings that name a specific file and function, run one extra bounded round in which the planner must settle each finding by reading that code. Keep the best plan between rounds so a near-complete plan is not lost. For plans that classify an outcome from records (landed, unlanded, taken by host), require a short evidence table: the source record or field, how it is written, and its value when the source is missing. For plans that change a core flow, require a list of every existing path through it (retry of a blocked job, parallel and serial drain, all RealSteps callers).
proposed_request: Hold a line after two non-landed attempts instead of retrying it. After two attempts on one request line that did not land, the drain must stop retrying that line and hold it for the person running Athena, instead of queuing another retry. Outcome: a request line with two non-landed attempts is held, and a third attempt is not started. Decide whether the host took a job from the pull-request link's own `state` field (merged or not), as written at pr.rs:360, and not from a missing landing record. The local records branch can be missing and reads as empty (store.rs:260-262), so a missing landing record alone must never count a job as unlanded. A job that has not landed on the host does not close its text line, and this applies to the hold's grouping only; the signal callers keep the existing wrapper. The hold check must not refuse the free landing retry of the item's own blocked job. Update every production RealSteps caller, including those in main.rs. Acceptance: (1) with two non-landed attempts on a line, the production drain::drain and drain::plan hold the line and start no third attempt; (2) a job whose pull-request link state shows merged counts as landed even when the records branch is missing; (3) a blocked job's free landing retry still runs; (4) one test covers the default serial drain and one covers max_concurrency > 1; (5) no other behavior changes. Cite line numbers only as hints and resolve each function against the current code before use.
